recap.title: index.js is the entry point
recap.body: Its top-level code runs once on load: build the page, check the session, register the service worker.

recap.title: Skeleton first, data second
recap.body: component() builds empty containers. restoreFromStorage() fills them.

recap.title: Local paint, then cloud
recap.body: The screen draws from localStorage before Supabase answers, so the app opens instantly.

recap.title: Boot runs once
recap.body: bootApp guards itself, so a second auth event can't start the app twice.

steps.title: The page skeleton is built first.
steps.why: Before anyone is signed in, index.js builds the whole page and attaches it to the body.

steps.title: component() makes the empty layout.
steps.why: Nav bar, sidebar, list and footer are created here, still with no projects in them.

steps.title: Signed in? Boot. Otherwise, the sign-in modal.
steps.why: The saved session decides the path. No session means the sign-in form covers the page.

steps.title: bootApp paints from localStorage first.
steps.why: Your projects appear straight away from this device's copy. The cloud catches up after.

steps.title: restoreFromStorage draws the sidebar and list.
steps.why: One sidebar row per project, then the selected project's todos in the main list.

steps.title: Then sync: migrate, hydrate, subscribe.
steps.why: Upload old local data once, pull everything from Supabase, then listen for live changes.

recap.title: One shared client
recap.body: supabaseClient.js makes the only Supabase client. Every file imports it.

recap.title: Missing keys never crash
recap.body: Without build-time keys a stub client answers with empty data.

recap.title: Email codes, no passwords
recap.body: sendCode emails a one-time code. verifyCode turns it into a session.

recap.title: The session gates every write
recap.body: persistMutation and hydrate both stop when nobody is signed in.

steps.title: One client, built from build-time keys.
steps.why: Webpack bakes the URL and public key in. The session is saved and refreshed for you.

steps.title: No keys? A stub keeps the app running.
steps.why: It answers every call with empty data, so a local build still opens, signed out.

match: return { ok: false, message: 'No account for that email' };
steps.title: Sign-in starts with an emailed code.
steps.why: Only existing accounts get one. Errors become short messages for the form.

steps.title: The code is swapped for a session.
steps.why: Supabase checks the code. On success the client now holds a signed-in session.

steps.title: Auth changes boot the app or tear it down.
steps.why: A new session hides the modal and boots. Signing out clears data and shows it again.

steps.title: Every write checks the session first.
steps.why: Projects carry your user_id. Todos don't: their access is checked through their project.

steps.title: Hydrate reads everything back.
steps.why: Your projects, then all todos you can see. The database only returns rows you own.

tours.title: Signing in for the first time

recap.title: Ask the cloud before onboarding
recap.body: A user with cloud projects skips the sample project and the tour.

recap.title: Migration runs once per user
recap.body: A marker in localStorage records that this device already uploaded.

recap.title: Cloud wins when it has data
recap.body: Local data only uploads into an empty account.

recap.title: Sign-out wipes this device
recap.body: Local projects and the marker go, so the next user starts clean.

steps.title: Boot first asks: do you already have data?
steps.why: The answer decides onboarding, and is passed on so the migration needn't ask again.

steps.title: Existing users skip the welcome.
steps.why: Cloud projects found? Onboarding is marked done. A timeout stops a slow check blocking the page.

steps.title: The probe fetches one project id.
steps.why: One row is enough to know. It returns null on errors, meaning 'couldn't tell'.

steps.title: Local data moves up once per user.
steps.why: Only into an empty account. The marker is set afterwards, so it never runs twice.

steps.title: Each project goes up, then its todos.
steps.why: Parents first, so every todo has a project to belong to. Blank rows are skipped.

steps.title: Signing out clears this device.
steps.why: Projects and the migration marker are removed, so the next person sees none of it.

recap.title: Memory first, always
recap.body: Edits change the item in memory straight away. Saving follows.

recap.title: Typing is batched
recap.body: saveToStorageSoon waits a moment, so a burst of keys is one write.

recap.title: dataChanged has no listeners
recap.body: Every local save fires it, but nothing listens yet, so a save alone repaints nothing.

recap.title: Two names for every field
recap.body: toTodoRowPayload maps tit / desc / due to title / description / due_date.

recap.title: Parents land first
recap.body: A todo write waits for its project's insert to finish.

steps.title: Each keystroke updates the item in memory.
steps.why: The title changes on the item right away. The save to disk is asked for, not done.

steps.title: Saves while typing are combined.
steps.why: One timer at a time: fast typing becomes a single write instead of one per key.

steps.title: All projects go to localStorage.
steps.why: Everything is written under one key, then dataChanged fires. No listener exists yet, so nothing repaints.

steps.title: Memory names become column names.
steps.why: The app says tit, desc and due. The database says title, description and due_date.

steps.title: A todo waits for its project to exist.
steps.why: If the project's insert is still in flight, the todo write waits, so it's never orphaned.

steps.title: Insert or update, and note our own echo.
steps.why: New rows insert, edits update. noteSelfEcho lets realtime skip the copy we just sent.

recap.title: Realtime updates the data
recap.body: Supabase pushes each change; listLogic applies it to memory and storage.

recap.title: Re-sync repaints the screen
recap.body: hydrateFromSupabase pulls everything, then fires listLogicHydrated.

recap.title: Never while you type
recap.body: A re-sync is skipped while an input has focus.

recap.title: Last write wins
recap.body: When both sides changed, the newer updated_at is kept.

steps.title: Two live channels: projects and todos.
steps.why: Supabase pushes every insert, update and delete on those tables to this device.

steps.title: A pushed change is applied to memory.
steps.why: Our own echoes are skipped. Others are added, updated or removed, then saved locally.

steps.title: A full re-sync, but never while you type.
steps.why: Repainting would wipe a half-typed edit, so focus in an input skips this round.

steps.title: When re-syncs happen.
steps.why: Tab visible again, window focus or back online. A 5-minute timer is the backstop.

steps.title: Merge: last write wins.
steps.why: The newer side wins. Local todos the server hasn't confirmed yet are kept, not lost.

match: restoreFromStorage({ fromSync: true, selectProject: activeProject || undefined });
steps.title: The screen repaints, same project selected.
steps.why: Sidebar and list are rebuilt from the merged data, keeping the project you had open.

recap.title: The service worker caches the build
recap.body: Files load from cache, so the app opens offline. The page itself checks the network first.

recap.title: A new build waits
recap.body: It installs in the background and waits until you choose to reload.

recap.title: Two cues, one path
recap.body: The mobile pill and the About row both call applyPendingUpdate.

recap.title: Only the tapping tab reloads
recap.body: Other open tabs get a 'Reload to finish' cue instead.

steps.title: The service worker caches the whole build.
steps.why: Old caches are dropped. Pages try the network first; everything else loads from cache.

steps.title: The page registers it and watches for builds.
steps.why: A new worker waiting means an update. Checks run on load, on return and hourly.

steps.title: Checks can also be forced.
steps.why: When a run ships, the assistant asks for a check now instead of waiting for the next poll.

steps.title: Phones get an 'Update available' pill.
steps.why: It sits above the bottom nav, appears once, and stays away for the session if dismissed.

steps.title: Settings › About shows the same cue.
steps.why: The Version row gets its own pill. Tapping it takes the same path as the mobile one.

steps.title: Both cues share one reload path.
steps.why: Mark this tab as the one that asked, then tell the waiting worker to take over.

steps.title: The new worker takes over; this tab reloads.
steps.why: Only the tab that asked reloads. Other open tabs get a 'Reload to finish' cue instead.

recap.title: listLogic is the only thing that changes data
recap.body: UI code edits the item, then asks listLogic to save it.

recap.title: Two places hold your data
recap.body: localStorage first (instant), Supabase second through persistMutation.

recap.title: One blank row, always
recap.body: Real in memory, never saved to the database.

recap.title: Two names for every field
recap.body: Memory says tit / desc / due. The database says title / description / due_date.

recap.title: Sync has two layers
recap.body: Realtime updates the data. Re-sync repaints the screen.

steps.title: One empty row always sits on top.
steps.why: It's a real item in memory, but it never gets saved to the server.

steps.title: Typing doesn't save the empty row.
steps.why: A half-typed title can't become a task if you switch projects mid-word.

steps.title: Enter: save locally, then insert or update.
steps.why: First commit inserts. Later edits update. Re-inserting used to cause duplicate errors.

steps.title: The row gets an id and is sent off.
steps.why: Blank titles are refused here too, so the empty row can never slip through.

steps.title: The one door to the database.
steps.why: Every write in the app passes here. Signed out? It stops, and the task stays local.

steps.title: A fresh empty row appears.
steps.why: The cursor jumps into it, so you can type the next task right away.

steps.title: Other devices receive the new row.
steps.why: The device that made it ignores its own echo. Others save it locally.

steps.title: Their screen repaints on re-sync.
steps.why: Not instantly: when the tab becomes visible again, or every 5 minutes.

recap.title: Typing stays local
recap.body: Title and description keystrokes change memory and batch a localStorage save.

recap.title: Two exits reach the server
recap.body: Enter on a title, or leaving the description, calls editToDoItem.

recap.title: Updates send the whole row
recap.body: persistMutation rewrites every column of the todo by id.

recap.title: Escape undoes the description
recap.body: It restores the text from when you started, then saves that.

steps.title: Typing a title edits it in memory.
steps.why: Each keystroke sets item.tit and asks for a batched local save. Nothing goes to the server yet.

steps.title: A burst of keys becomes one write.
steps.why: While a timer is pending, further calls do nothing. When it fires, one save covers them all.

steps.title: Enter sends the new title to the server.
steps.why: On a row that already exists, Enter saves locally at once, then calls editToDoItem.

steps.title: Descriptions save locally as you type.
steps.why: The panel text goes into item.desc untrimmed, so line breaks and indents survive.

steps.title: Leaving the description syncs it.
steps.why: Blur saves at once and sends the update. Ctrl+Enter and Escape both end in a blur.

steps.title: editToDoItem asks for an update.
steps.why: No id or no title means no write. Otherwise the whole item is mapped to a database row.

steps.title: The row is overwritten by id.
steps.why: Every column is written, not just the edited one. The echo is noted so realtime skips it.

recap.title: Status and done are separate
recap.body: The badge sets Active, In Progress or Idea. The checkbox sets completed.

recap.title: One write path each
recap.body: setToDoStatus and setToDoCompleted save locally, then update the server.

recap.title: Repaint in place
recap.body: Only the badge and row class change; the list re-sorts without rebuilding rows.

recap.title: Done sinks to the bottom
recap.body: sortCompletedToBottom keeps open tasks above finished ones.

steps.title: One listener handles every status badge.
steps.why: Pipeline badges like Review or Asking open other views. A plain status badge opens the menu.

steps.title: The menu offers Active, In Progress, Idea.
steps.why: It closes on a choice, an outside click, Escape, resize or scroll.

steps.title: Picking one: save, repaint, re-sort.
steps.why: The choice goes through listLogic, the badge repaints, and the list re-sorts and re-filters.

steps.title: setToDoStatus saves locally, then remotely.
steps.why: Unknown or unchanged values are ignored. Committed rows also send an update.

steps.title: Only the badge and row class repaint.
steps.why: No full re-render, so anything else in progress on the row is left alone.

steps.title: Checking a task off is its own path.
steps.why: The checkbox sets completed through setToDoCompleted, not the status menu.

steps.title: After the animation, the row moves down.
steps.why: The data is re-sorted first, then the existing row element moves to its new slot.

steps.title: Blank row, open tasks, then done ones.
steps.why: If the order already fits, it stops. Otherwise every real task gets a new position on the server.

recap.title: Dates are m-d-y text
recap.body: item.due holds a string like 4-24-2026, or empty for none.

recap.title: Picking saves locally
recap.body: setItemDue writes localStorage and recolors the row straight away.

recap.title: Closing reaches the server
recap.body: Every close commits Repeat, which sends the whole row.

recap.title: Urgency is computed
recap.body: Overdue and due-soon come from today’s date, never stored.

steps.title: The date pill opens a calendar.
steps.why: Tapping the pill toggles a date popover anchored to that row.

steps.title: Quick dates, a month grid and Repeat.
steps.why: Today, Tomorrow and +1w sit above the grid. A Repeat section and Clear sit below.

steps.title: Six weeks of days, each a button.
steps.why: Clicking a day writes that date to the task and closes the popover.

steps.title: setItemDue stores the date locally.
steps.why: The date is saved as m-d-y text, the row recolors, then todoDueDateChanged fires.

steps.title: Overdue and soon get their own colors.
steps.why: Past due marks the row overdue; three days or less marks it soon. Done tasks get neither.

steps.title: The pill says it in words.
steps.why: No date reads 'Set date'. Otherwise '2d overdue', 'Due today', 'Due in 3d' or the date itself.

steps.title: Sorted by due? The list reorders.
steps.why: Only while the Due sort is on. Rows move in place, so open panels come with them.

steps.title: Closing the popover commits Repeat.
steps.why: Every close runs this. setRecurrence sends the whole row, so the new date reaches the server too.

recap.title: Two ways to delete
recap.body: The × button confirms first. A left swipe deletes and offers undo.

recap.title: Delete by reference
recap.body: removeToDoByItem matches the item itself, never its title.

recap.title: Undo is a fresh insert
recap.body: insertToDoAt puts the same item back and inserts it again on the server.

recap.title: Five seconds to change your mind
recap.body: One toast at a time; a new one replaces the old.

steps.title: The × button asks first.
steps.why: A confirm modal names the task. Only after you confirm is it removed.

steps.title: The list redraws and focus stays put.
steps.why: The row that moves into the deleted slot gets focus, so arrow keys keep their place.

steps.title: removeToDoByItem removes that exact item.
steps.why: Matching the object, not the title, means a duplicate title can't delete the wrong row.

steps.title: The server row is deleted by id.
steps.why: It's noted as our own echo first, so realtime doesn't apply it a second time here.

steps.title: Swiping left skips the modal.
steps.why: The slot is remembered, the item removed, and an undo toast shown instead of a confirm.

steps.title: One toast at a time, for five seconds.
steps.why: A new toast replaces the old one. UNDO runs the callback; otherwise the toast goes on its own.

steps.title: UNDO puts it back where it was.
steps.why: The remembered slot is passed back to listLogic, then the list redraws.

steps.title: insertToDoAt inserts it again.
steps.why: A double tap can't add it twice. The same item goes back to the server as a new insert.

recap.title: One drag helper
recap.body: setupRowDrag serves task rows and project rows alike.

recap.title: Mouse and touch share the maths
recap.body: Both use computeDropIndex and hand the result to onReorder.

recap.title: Done and open never mix
recap.body: A drop is clamped so it stays on its own side of the boundary.

recap.title: Positions sync
recap.body: reorderToDo and reorderProject send every new position to the server.

steps.title: One helper drags tasks and projects.
steps.why: setupRowDrag puts the same native drag events on any row. Rows that can't drag cancel the start.

steps.title: A line shows where the row will land.
steps.why: Each dragover moves the indicator and scrolls the list near its edges.

steps.title: The drop slot is counted by midpoints.
steps.why: Each row whose middle is above the pointer adds one. Done and open tasks never swap sides.

match: const toIdx    = computeDropIndex(dragging, cfg.container, cfg.itemSelector, event.clientY);
steps.title: Dropping hands two indexes to the owner.
steps.why: From and to go to onReorder. The drag helper itself never touches the data.

match: armTimer: canDrag ? setTimeout(function() { state.armed = true; }, TOUCH_ARM_MS) : null
steps.title: On touch, a short hold arms the drag.
steps.why: Hold 180ms before moving. Moving sooner scrolls, or swipes sideways. Lifting runs the same drop maths.

steps.title: Tasks: reorder the data, then the rows.
steps.why: The rows follow the model, not where you let go, so a clamped drop still draws correctly.

steps.title: reorderToDo saves every new position.
steps.why: The blank row is set aside, the move applied, then each real task's position goes to the server.

steps.title: Projects reorder the same way.
steps.why: Sidebar drags call reorderProject, which rebuilds the project order and updates each one's position.

recap.title: One create path
recap.body: The + button and the picker both end in the same Enter handler.

recap.title: Names are unique keys
recap.body: A name already in use turns red and nothing is created.

recap.title: Projects insert first
recap.body: Todos written meanwhile wait for the project row to exist.

recap.title: New means selected
recap.body: The new project is highlighted and its empty list drawn.

steps.title: The + button adds an empty sidebar row.
steps.why: It switches to the projects view and appends a 'New Project' input for you to name.

steps.title: Enter checks the name is new.
steps.why: A name that already exists turns red and the handler stops there.

steps.title: A new name goes to addProject.
steps.why: The first Enter creates; later ones rename. Then the row is selected and its list drawn.

steps.title: The picker reuses the same path.
steps.why: createProjectByName clicks + and presses Enter for you, so the result is identical.

steps.title: addProject stores it with a fresh id.
steps.why: Empty names are refused. The project starts with one blank row, saves locally, then inserts.

steps.title: The insert is remembered while in flight.
steps.why: The project's insert promise is kept by id until the database answers.

steps.title: Its todos wait for it.
steps.why: A todo written for that project awaits the insert, so it never points at a missing project.

steps.title: selectProjectRow highlights the new row.
steps.why: The old selection is cleared and the list takes the project's accent color.

recap.title: Filters hide, never remove
recap.body: applyTaskFilter only adds a hidden class to rows.

recap.title: One definition per filter
recap.body: Counts and visibility use the same match functions.

recap.title: Sorting is drawing only
recap.body: Your manual order is never overwritten by a sort.

recap.title: Both are remembered
recap.body: The chosen filter and sort are kept in localStorage.

steps.title: One bar, one click handler.
steps.why: Desktop pills and the mobile cycle pill all route through one listener that saves the choice.

steps.title: Three filters, each a match function.
steps.why: All is every open task. In progress and Done also read the pipeline phase. Checked-off tasks match none.

match: return PHASE_FILTERS.filter(function (f) { return f.key === key; })[0] || PHASE_FILTERS[0];
steps.title: Unknown keys fall back to All.
steps.why: So a stale saved value still gives a working filter.

steps.title: applyTaskFilter hides rows in place.
steps.why: Counts and visibility come from the same match functions. Rows just get a hidden class.

steps.title: The sort menu: None, Due date, Status.
steps.why: Desktop gets this dropdown, phones a bottom sheet. Both call applyTaskSortChoice.

steps.title: Choosing a sort saves it and redraws.
steps.why: The sort is stored, the list rebuilt in the new order, then the filter applied again.

steps.title: Sorting only changes the drawing order.
steps.why: Due and Status return a sorted copy. None returns your manual order, untouched.

steps.title: Every redraw re-applies the filter.
steps.why: Rows are appended in sort order, then applyTaskFilter hides the ones the filter excludes.

recap.title: Chips live on the blank row
recap.body: Today, Tomorrow, a calendar and a description toggle.

recap.title: The date lands on commit
recap.body: A due chip is only a choice until Enter stamps it.

recap.title: Everything ends in Enter
recap.body: Voice and paste both fire a synthetic Enter on the title input.

recap.title: Pastes start in progress
recap.body: The whole paste becomes the description; the status is In Progress.

steps.title: The blank row grows a strip of chips.
steps.why: Only the empty 'Add a task' row gets them: Today, Tomorrow, a calendar and a description toggle.

steps.title: A due chip only records your choice.
steps.why: Today and Tomorrow set chosenDueChip. The calendar chip opens the normal date popover.

steps.title: Enter stamps the chosen day.
steps.why: Committing a dateless task calls this: Today is offset 0, Tomorrow 1. Custom already wrote its date.

steps.title: The mic presses Enter for you.
steps.why: When dictation commits, onFinal fires a synthetic Enter, since iOS can't reopen the keyboard.

steps.title: startDictation streams words into the field.
steps.why: Each result rewrites the input live. A watchdog ends a session left running.

steps.title: Tapping again commits what was heard.
steps.why: It stops without cancelling, so finishSession calls onFinal, but only if words were heard.

steps.title: Pasting: a checkbox line becomes the title.
steps.why: With no checkbox line, the first non-empty line is used. The whole paste is the description.

steps.title: The paste goes through the same Enter.
steps.why: Description and an In Progress status are set first, then a synthetic Enter commits it.
